Individualized Honors Programs (IHP) and Single Gender Academies are also available. These programs are designed to expand college access and success and offer rigorous, student-centered programs that blend high school and college coursework with some programs providing the

opportunity to earn an AA degree. Students outside of the resident attendance boundary and Los Angeles Unified boundaries may apply. INFORMATION 4 HOW DOES THE CHOICES PROCESS WORK? There is a unique selection process for each Choices program. For information, please refer to the following sections: MAGNET PROGRAMS | PAGES 16-38 SCHOOLS FOR ADV ANCED STUDIES | PAGES 54-60 PERMITS WITH TRANSPORT ATION | PAGES 39-40 EARL Y/MIDDLE COLLEGES | PAGES 61-62 MUL TILINGUAL MUL TICUL TURAL PROGRAMS| PAGES 41-53 AFFILIA TED CHARTER SCHOOLS | PAGES 63-66 HOW TO APPLY FOR CHOICES PROGRAMS? Pick Your Programs: Applicants can apply for up to six programs and multiple schools within each program on just one application.

Do Your Research: Before applying, it is a good idea to contact the school in which you are interested. The school can tell you about information sessions, tours, uniforms, and transportation (if available). Only Apply to Programs You Want to Attend: Applicants that apply to more than one choice per program, and are not selected, will ONLY be waitlisted for their first choice (except Affiliated Charter Schools).  Second and third choices are optional.  Current magnet students that apply to another magnet program and are selected will automatically lose their seat regardless of

whether or not they accept. Check the Eligibility Requirements: Make sure to check the eligibility requirements and verification procedures for each program before applying. Some programs have extra steps to verify if the applicant meets the requirements. Apply On-time: Apply online at Choices.LAUSD.net .The on-time application for the next school year is October 1st through November 6, 2026. ALREADY ENROLLED IN ACHOICES PROGRAM? New Application: If the applicant was on a waiting list last year and wants another opportunity, or wants to switch programs, they will need a new application.

Applicants also need to apply if they are culminating, i.e. from elementary to middle school. Already Enrolled: If the applicant is already in a Choices program and wants to stay there, they do not need a new application. HAVE SIBLINGS? Twins and Triplets: If the applicant is a twin or triplet, all siblings need to live at the same address. Twins/triplets must submit separate applications to the same program (first choice only) in the same year to be placed consecutively during the selection process. Sibling Priority: Sibling priority only applies to currently enrolled siblings of students that will attend the same program next school year.

To receive sibling priority, applicant(s) need to list all of the siblings on the application. Siblings must live at the same address. Make sure the address is correct in the system before the application deadline. READY TO START SCHOOL? Check Available Grade Levels: Not all Choices elementary programs offer Transitional Kindergarten (TK). A list of schools that offer TK is in the Choices Brochure. Age-Grade Eligibility is required for Transitional Kindergarten, Kindergarten, and 1st Grade.  Transitional Kindergarten (TK): TK is a two-year Kindergarten program for children turning 4 by September 1st.

 Kindergarten: Kindergartners must turn 5 by September 1st.  First Grade: First graders must turn 6 by September 1st. ADDITIONAL INFORMATION Applications: If multiple applications are submitted for the same applicant, only the first one is considered. Attend: If the applicant is not enrolled and attending school by the first week, they will lose their Choices seat. Double-Check Y our Application: It is up to the applicant to make sure that all information is correct.

INFORMATION 55 What Ha WHAT HAPPENS AFTER APPLYING? Selection/Waiting List Notification: During early February, all on-time applicants with eligible choices will receive a Selection/Waiting List Notification email. Selected Applicants: "Selected" means that the applicant has been offered a seat to a Choices program. The selected applicant must accept or decline the offer online or by contacting the school.  Selected applicants can only accept ONE Choices placement.  If the applicant is selected into another program and accepts it, they will be dropped automatically from their current placement.

For Magnet Programs ONLY: If the applicant is selected into another magnet program, they will be dropped automatically from their current magnet program regardless if the placement is accepted or declined.  If an applicant is selected to a program and accepts the offer, this will not affect the applicant's waitlist status for other programs.  If no response is received by the deadline, it is considered a decline. All declines are final. Waitlisted Applicants: "Waiting List" means that the applicant has been placed on the school's waitlist.

Applicants will be placed on a waitlist for their first-choice only (within each program). Affiliated Charter Schools will put the applicant on a waitlist for all the schools to which they applied.  The applicant will be contacted directly by the school ONLY if a waitlist seat becomes available and the applicant is next on the list.  A waitlist seat may be offered up until the fourth week of the first semester or the second week of the second semester. Exceptions: Multilingual Multicultural Programs and Affiliated Charter School applicants remain on the waiting list until the end of the academic

year to which they applied (see program information for details). NEED TO MAKE ACORRECTION OR CHANGE? Online Updates: Applicants can update their online application until November 6, 2026. Application Withdrawals and Corrections: Email ApplyforSchools@lausd.net by December 18, 2026, or mail the request to Choices, P.O. Box 513307, Los Angeles, CA 90051. MISSED THE CHOICES ON-TIME DEADLINE? Late Choices applications for the 2027-28 school year are accepted starting December 1, 2026.  Late applications will be added to the end of the waiting list.  The school will only contact you if a seat opens up and your child is next on the waiting list.

A waitlist seat may be offered up until the fourth week of the first semester or the second week of the second semester. Exceptions: Multilingual Multicultural Programs and Affiliated Charter School applicants remain on the waiting list until the end of the academic year to which they applied (see program information for details). Applying late to additional schools will not affect your on-time application. Late applicants can apply to as many programs as they want, but each choice requires a separate application. Late applicants to Gifted/Highly Gifted Magnet Programs and Schools for Advanced Studies (SAS) must meet required, program specific

criteria, however, verification of eligibility is processed at the school site.  Verification of Eligibility forms for late applicants, if applicable, must be submitted directly to the school of choice when the parent/ guardian is contacted by the school about an available seat. For more information, visit: Choices.LAUSD.net. TRANSPORTATION Transportation may be available for students residing within Los Angeles Unified boundaries. Please visit the Transportation Services Division website at www.lausd.org/transportation or log into Parent Portal to complete the opt-in process. You may also contact the school to inquire about transportation options. NEED HELP? Need Help? To learn more about specific schools, please contact the program(s) you are interested in for more information. For application support, call the Choices Support Line at (213) 241-4177 or email applyforschools@lausd.net.

INFORMATION 6 CRITERIA FOR GIFTED/HIGHL YGIFTED MAGNET PROGRAMS AND SCHOOLS FOR ADV ANCED STUDIES To be eligible for Gifted/Highly Gifted Magnet Programs or Schools for Advanced Studies (SAS), students must meet the applicable program eligibility criteria and complete all required verification processes by the stated deadlines. Applications will not be included in the selection process if eligibility requirements are not met by the deadline. Students must live within Los Angeles Unified School District (LAUSD) boundaries at the time of application and while participating in the program, with the exception of applicants to

SAS Single Gender Academies and Individualized Honors Programs (IHP), which are open to students living outside LAUSD boundaries. ELIGIBILITY FOR HIGHL YGIFTED MAGNET PROGRAMS To be eligible for Highly Gifted Magnet Programs, students must be identified by LAUSD as: Highly Gifted (HG): Scoring at the 99.9 percentile rank on an Intellectual Ability assessment administered by a designated LAUSD GA TE psychologist OROR Highly Gifted Applicable (HGA): Scoring at the 99.5 to 99.8 percentile rank on an Intellectual Ability assessment administered by a designated LAUSD GA TE psychologist. Upon receipt of the application, the District will automatically check LAUSD records for eligibility.

If the applicant was identified as HG or HGA in LAUSD and is currently attending a private school (including in-home private school), independent charter or other non-LAUSD school, the parent/guardian must submit a Verification of Eligibility form to ensure that the applicant is included in the LAUSD database (see Verification). Parents/guardians may email Gifted/T alented Programs at GA TE@lausd.net to confirm if the student is eligible to apply to a Highly Gifted Magnet Program. Students must be assessed and identified as HG or HGA before the deadline to be eligible for on-time

application and selection. ELIGIBILITY FOR GIFTED MAGNET PROGRAMS AND SCHOOLS FOR ADV ANCED STUDIES (SAS) To be eligible for Gifted Magnet Programs or Schools for Advanced Studies (SAS), a student must meet one of the following criteria before the deadline: A The student has been identified by LAUSD as gifted in one of the following categories: Intellectual Ability (including gifted, highly gifted, or highly gifted applicable) High Achievement Ability Specific Academic Ability Creative Ability Leadership Ability Upon receipt of the application, the District will automatically check LAUSD records for eligibility.

If a student was previously identified by LAUSD but is currently attending a private school (including in-home private school), independent charter school, or other non-LAUSD school, a Verification of Eligibility form must be submitted so the student can be included in the LAUSD database OROR B The student received national percentile scores of 85 or above or Advanced/Standard Exceeded on a District-approved standardized achievement test OROR C The student demonstrates the ability to meet ALL FOUR critical thinking and problem-solving skills (in primary language):  Explain meanings or relationships among facts, information, or concepts that demonstrate depth and complexity

 Formulate new ideas or solutions and elaborate on the information  Use alternative methods in approaching new or unfamiliar mathematical problems  Use extensive vocabulary easily and accurately to express creative ideas The student's school determines whether the student demonstrates all four skills, shows the ability or strong potential to work two years above grade level in academic subjects, and, for SAS kindergarten applicants, meets the applicable kindergarten eligibility requirements. The eligibility recommendation submitted by the principal of the student's current school is final. Late verification will

not be accepted for on-time applicants. ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENT FOR INDIVIDUALIZED HONORS PROGRAMS (IHP) Students applying to an Individualized Honors Program (IHP) must: Meet one of the SAS eligibility criteria above ANDAND Receive an eligible score on the IHP assessment (see IHP section)

INFORMATION 7 VERIFICA TION PROCEDURES If your child is not currently identified as gifted by LAUSD (criterion A), eligibility may be verified through standardized achievement test data (criterion B) or demonstrated critical thinking and problem-solving skills (criterion C). Students applying to a new school/program or transitioning from elementary school to middle school, or middle school to high school, must be reverified by their current school as eligible to continue in a Gifted Magnet Program or School for Advanced Studies (SAS). Review the section below that corresponds to your

child's current school enrollment status. CURRENT LAUSD STUDENTS Students currently enrolled in an LAUSD school do not need to submit a Verification of Eligibility form. Upon receipt of the application, the District will automatically check LAUSD records for eligibility. Families may contact their child's current LAUSD school if they have questions about eligibility. STUDENTS APPL YING FROM APRIV ATE SCHOOL, INDEPENDENT CHARTER SCHOOL, OR OTHER NON-LAUSD SCHOOL Parents/guardians must ensure that the student's current school submits the required Verification of Eligibility form by the deadline. This requirement also applies to incoming kindergarten SAS applicants attending a non-LAUSD preschool or transitional kindergarten (TK).

1 Visit Choices.LAUSD.net (select Magnet or SAS and click "Who is eligible?") to download the Verification of Eligibility (SAS Kindergarten) form or Verification of Eligibility (Grades 1-12) form, or call (213) 241-4177 to request the form. 2 Complete the student and parent information sections, sign and date. 3 Provide the form to your child's current school so school staff can complete the required sections. 4 Once completed, school personnel (not the parent/guardian) must email the signed Verification of Eligibility form to giftedverification@lausd.net no later than November 20, 2026.

The school will receive an email confirmation when the form is received. Important Reminders To be considered for selection, parents/guardians are responsible for ensuring:  A Choices application is submitted by November 6, 2026 ANDAND  The student's current school submits the Verification of Eligibility form by November 20, 2026 A Verification of Eligibility form is not an application. Late forms will not be accepted for on-time application and selection. STUDENTS APPL YING FROM AN IN-HOME PRIV ATE SCHOOL (PRIV ATE SCHOOL AFFIDA VIT) OR NOT ENROLLED IN SCHOOL

An alternate verification process is available for in-home private school applicants without a verifying organization and kindergarten SAS applicants who are not enrolled in preschool or TK. This process includes submitting evidence demonstrating the student’s advanced skills, characteristics, and potential. Parents/guardians must email GA TE@lausd.net with the subject line "Verification Process" no later than November 20, 2026, to request the verification. Important Reminders To be considered for selection, parents/guardians are responsible for ensuring:  A Choices application is submitted by November 6, 2026 ANDAND  The alternate verification process is requested by emailing GA TE@lausd.net by November 20, 2026 Late requests will not be accepted for on-time application and selection.

MAGNET PROGRAMS INFORMATION 17 WHAT ARE MAGNET PROGRAMS? The Los Angeles Unified magnet schools/centers are voluntary programs established through an integration court-order to address the five harms of racial isolation: Low Academic Achievement, Low Self-Esteem, Lack of Access to Post-Secondary Opportunities, Interracial Hostility and Intolerance and Overcrowded Conditions. Some magnets are full school programs while others are located in residential schools with access to all activities and experiences. WHAT ARE THE GOALS OF THE INSTRUCTIONAL PROGRAM? Magnets provide rigorous, high-quality, theme-based instruction in alignment with the Los Angeles Unified’s goals: 100 percent

graduation, proficiency for all, 100 percent attendance, parent, community and student engagement, school safety, and building a solid foundation for early learners. Each magnet falls within one of seven instructional themes: Career and Social Entrepreneurship, Centers for Enriched Studies, Gifted and Highly Gifted, Liberal Arts, New Media, Science/Technology or Visual and Performing Arts. The earliest grade offered is kindergarten. However, most magnet schools offer a non-magnet Transitional Kindergarten (TK) as part of their residential program with the exception of: 32nd Street/USC, Academy for Enriched Sciences, Arroyo Seco, Balboa, Community,

Lake Balboa, Melrose, Mid-City, Open, Point Fermin, South Shores, Vintage, and Westside. WHO IS ELIGIBLE? All students in grades K-12 and residing within the Los Angeles Unified boundary are eligible to apply including English Learners, Standard English Learners, students with disabilities, and gifted/talented students. Post office boxes are not accepted. Only Gifted and Highly Gifted Magnets (pages 23-26) require specific eligibility criteria (pages 6-7) for selection. Magnet programs require parents to mark ONE federally identified ethnicity/race category on the application to be processed. HOW ARE STUDENTS SELECTED? The on-time student selection process is based on the Magnet Priority Point System and the need to maintain a racially balanced

enrollment, and by available space. It is the parents/guardians responsibility to verify the student’s address, grade and ethnicity prior to the application deadline. APPLICATION GUIDELINES AND SELECTION PROCESS: Do not submit a new application if your child is currently enrolled in a magnet and wishes to continue at the same magnet. Applicants currently enrolled in a magnet who apply and are selected for another magnet will automatically be dropped from their current magnet, whether they accept or decline. Y ou may apply to up to three different magnet programs.

The second and third choices are optional. Magnet Priority Points are considered for each magnet choice and used when selected to a magnet. If not selected to their first choice, the applicant will be considered for their second and/or third choice, if any. If selected to any one of their choices, the applicant will not be on the waiting list for the other choice(s). If not selected into a magnet, the applicant will be placed on the waiting list for their first choice only. COMPTON UNIFIED SCHOOL DISTRICT (CUSD) APPLICANTS

Transportation is available to some magnet programs. BEFORE MAKING YOUR SELECTION, contact the school or Transportation Services to determine if the magnet program offers transportation and if the closest pick-up/drop-off point is a reasonable distance from your home. Routes and pick-up/drop-off locations have been established for the 2027-2028 school year. No new stops will be added. For information about existing bus routes, contact Transportation Services Division at 1-800-LABUSES or (213) 580-2900. Students attending the following span schools have a one-mile eligibility radius: 32nd Street/USC, Arroyo Seco, Lake Balboa, Laurel, Menlo, Sherman Oaks CES, Western Ave and Westside. Students with disabilities enrolling in a Magnet Program may also have access to transportation. Magnet programs may offer school to school transportation for eligible students. DUAL LANGUAGE EDUCATION PROGRAMS INFORMATION 42 WHAT ARE DUAL LANGUAGE EDUCATION PROGRAMS? The goal of Dual Language Education (DLE) programs is to have students become bilingual, biliterate, and respectful of different cultures. During the instructional day students engage in learning language arts, math, science and other content areas. WHAT ARE THE GOALS OF THE INSTRUCTIONAL PROGRAM? Los Angeles Unified School District offers more than 230 DLE programs for students from Transitional Kindergarten through 12th grade. Students can learn Arabic, Armenian, French, Japanese, Korean, Mandarin, or Spanish. These programs help students build language skills,

succeed in school, and become leaders in their communities and the world. Students can also earn awards as they learn new languages. They may receive awards in TK, kindergarten, 1st, 3rd, 5th, and 8th grades. In 12th grade, students who show strong skills in two or more languages can earn the State Seal of Biliteracy from the California Department of Education. WHO IS ELIGIBLE? Reclassified Fluent English Proficient (RFEP): Students who were previously classified as English Learners and have demonstrated proficiency and fluency in English. English Only (EO): Students whose home language is English. WHAT ARE SCHOOLS FOR ADVANCED STUDIES? Schools for Advanced Studies (SAS) are Los Angeles Unified schools that have received a designation for equitable and exemplary Gifted and T alented Education (GA TE) programs. WHAT ARE THE GOALS OF THE INSTRUCTIONAL PROGRAM? All Los Angeles Unified schools have GA TE programs in grades K–12 designed to support gifted, talented, and advanced students. As exemplary GA TE models, SAS schools help gifted and advanced learners reach their fullest potential by providing differentiated instruction with depth, complexity, novelty, and acceleration. SAS schools also provide challenging and supportive learning

environments, GA TE family engagement, and ongoing professional learning for teachers focused on the unique academic and social- emotional needs of gifted, talented, and advanced students from diverse backgrounds. WHO IS ELIGIBLE? Students must be verified as meeting SAS eligibility criteria to participate. Detailed criteria and directions are available at choices.lausd.net and gate.lausd.org. Students in grades Pre-K–11 who live within an SAS school’s attendance area can enroll without submitting a Choices application; these students are automatically included in the school’s SAS/GA TE program if they meet SAS criteria.

Students in grades Pre-K–11 who live outside an SAS school’s attendance area, but within Los Angeles Unified boundaries, may apply through the Choices process if they meet SAS criteria. Applicants who are currently enrolled in non-district schools – including private schools and independent charter schools – must submit an application and the required verification form by the published deadlines. Applicants who are not enrolled in a school, preschool, or transitional kindergarten (TK) program, or who are enrolled in an in-home private school (Private School Affidavit), are required to submit an application and email Gifted/T alented Programs at

GA TE@lausd.net before the application deadline to request verification. KINDERGARTEN SAS ELIGIBILITY CRITERIA Incoming kindergarten applicants must show strong thinking and problem-solving skills. Eligibility must be verified by a preschool or TK administrator using SAS kindergarten readiness criteria. Detailed criteria and directions are available at gate.lausd.org. Applicants who are not enrolled in preschool or TK are required to submit an application and email Gifted/T alented Programs at GA TE@lausd.net before the application deadline to request verification. HOW ARE STUDENTS SELECTED? Students who live within the boundaries of the SAS school are placed first.

If space is available, eligible applicants from outside the school boundaries may be selected through the Choices process. If there are more eligible applicants than available spaces, a random, unbiased selection process will be conducted. Applicants who are siblings of current continuing students at the school receive priority, if space is available. HOW DO IAPPLY TO AN AFFILIATED CHARTER OR ZONES OF CHOICE SCHOOL WITH THE SAS DESIGNATION? Some Affiliated Charter Schools and Zones of Choice (ZOC) Schools have the SAS designation. Applications must be submitted through the Affiliated Charter or ZOC process.

Students who are selected or assigned to the school and meet SAS eligibility criteria will be included in the school’s SAS/GA TE program unless the parent/guardian opts out. Habilidad Intelectual administrada por un psicólogo designado por GA TE del LAUSD O O Altamente Dotado Aplicable (HGA, por sus siglas en inglés): obtener una puntuación en el rango percentil 99.5 - 99.8 en una evaluación de Habilidad Intelectual administrada por un psicólogo designado por GA TE del LAUSD.. solicitud presentada a tiempo y para participar en el proceso de selección. ¿QUÉ SON LOS PROGRAMAS MAGNET? Las escuelas/centros magnet del Distrito Escolar Unificado de Los Ángeles (LAUSD) son programas voluntarios establecidos mediante un decreto judicial con el propósito de reducir los cinco perjuicios causados por la segregación racial: rendimiento académico bajo, autoestima baja, falta de acceso a oportunidades de educación postsecundaria, hostilidad e intolerancia interracial, y escuelas sobrepobladas. Algunos programas magnet ocupan todo el plantel escolar, mientras que otros están ubicados dentro de escuelas de vecindario y ofrecen acceso a todas las actividades y experiencias de la escuela anfitriona.

¿CUÁLES SON LOS OBJETIVOS DEL PROGRAMA EDUCATIVO? Los programas magnet ofrecen una enseñanza rigurosa, de alta calidad basada en temas específicos, alineadas con los objetivos del Distrito Escolar Unificado de Los Ángeles: graduación del 100 % de los alumnos, dominio académico para todos, asistencia del 100 %, participación de padres y la comunidad, seguridad escolar y una base sólida para los aprendices más jóvenes. Cada programa magnet se enmarca en una de siete áreas temáticas de instrucción: Carrera Profesional y Emprendimiento Social, Centros de Estudios Enriquecidos, Educación para Alumnos

Dotados y Altamente Dotados, Artes Liberales, Medios de comunicación nuevos, Ciencia/tecnología/ingeniería/matemáticas, o Artes Visuales y Escénicas. El grado más temprano que se ofrece es el jardín de infancia (Kindergarten). Sin embargo, la mayoría de las escuelas magnet ofrecen un programa de Kindergarten de Transición (TK) que no forma parte del programa magnet y que se ofrece dentro de su programa residencial, con excepción de las siguientes escuelas: 32nd Street/USC, Academy for Enriched Sciences, Arroyo Seco, Balboa, Community, Lake Balboa, Melrose, Mid-City, Open, Point Fermin, South Shores, Vintage y Westside.

¿QUIÉN ES ELEGIBLE? Todos los alumnos de los grados K–12 que residen dentro de los límites del Distrito Escolar Unificado de Los Ángeles son elegibles para solicitar ingreso, incluidos los alumnos aprendices de inglés, los alumnos de inglés estándar, los alumnos con discapacidades y los alumnos dotados o talentosos. No se aceptan apartados postales (P .O. Boxes). Solo los programas Magnet para Alumnos Dotados y Altamente Dotados (páginas 23–26) requieren criterios específicos de elegibilidad (páginas 6–7) para la selección. Los programas magnet requieren que los padres o tutores indiquen una sola categoría de etnia/raza reconocida por el gobierno federal en la

solicitud para que la solicitud pueda ser procesada. ¿CÓMO SE SELECCIONA ALOS ALUMNOS? El proceso de selección de alumnos que presentan su solicitud dentro del plazo establecido se basa en el Sistema de Puntos de Prioridad Magnet, la necesidad de mantener una matrícula con equilibrio racial y la disponibilidad de espacios. Es responsabilidad de los padres o tutores verificar la dirección del alumno, el grado escolar y la información de etnia/raza antes de la fecha límite para presenter la solicitud. GUÍA DE SOLICITUD YPROCESO DE SELECCIÓN No presente una nueva solicitud si su hijo(a) ya está inscrito(a) en un programa magnet y desea continuar en el mismo programa.

Los solicitantes que actualmente están inscritos en un programa magnet y solicitan ingreso a otro programa magnet, y son seleccionados, serán declinados automáticamente de su programa magnet actual, independientemente de que acepten o rechacen la nueva selección. Puede solicitar admisión a un máximo de tres programas magnet diferentes. La segunda y la tercera opción son opcionales. Los Puntos de Prioridad Magnet se consideran para cada una de las opciones seleccionadas y se utilizan durante el proceso de asignación a un programa magnet. Si el solicitante no es seleccionado para su primera opción, será considerado para su segunda y/o tercera opción, si se aplica.

Si es seleccionado para cualquiera de sus opciones, no permanecerá en la lista de espera de las otras opciones. Si no es seleccionado para ningún programa magnet, será colocado únicamente en la lista de espera de su primera opción. INFORMACIÓN DE LOS PROGRAMAS DE EDUCACIÓN DE LENGUAJE DUAL 42 ¿ QUÉ SON LOS PROGRAMAS DE LA EDUCACIÓN DE LENGUAJE DUAL? El objetivo de los programas de Educación de Lenguaje Dual (DLE) es que los estudiantes lleguen a ser bilingües, alfabetizados en dos idiomas y respetuosos de las diferentes culturas. Durante el día escolar, los estudiantes participan en el aprendizaje de lengua y literatura, matemáticas, ciencias y otras áreas de contenido académico. ¿CUÁLES SON LOS OBJETIVOS DEL PROGRAMA EDUCATIVO? El Distrito Escolar Unificado de Los Angeles ofrece más de 230 programas de Educación en Dos Idiomas (DLE) para estudiantes desde

el Kindergarten de Transición (TK) hasta el 12.º grado. Los estudiantes pueden aprender árabe, armenio, francés, japonés, coreano, mandarín o español. Estos programas ayudan a los estudiantes a desarrollar habilidades lingüísticas, tener éxito en la escuela y convertirse en líderes en sus comunidades y en el mundo. Los estudiantes también pueden obtener reconocimientos a medida que aprenden nuevos idiomas. Pueden recibir premios en diferentes etapas como TK, kindergarten, 1.º, 3.º, 5.º y 8.º grado. En el 12.º grado, los estudiantes que demuestren competencia en dos o más idiomas pueden obtener el Sello Estatal del Alfabetización Bilingüe concedido por el Departamento Educativo de California.

¿ QUIÉN ES ELEGIBLE? Los programas de Educación de Lenguaje Dual (DLE) están diseñados para apoyar a una variedad de estudiante que hablan otros idiomas, incluyendo: Aprendices de inglés (EL): Estudiantes que están en proceso de aprender inglés como un idioma adicional. Inicialmente competente en inglés (IFEP): Estudiantes que demuestran competencia inicial en inglés pero que pueden necesitar apoyo para mantener y mejorar sus habilidades lingüísticas. Reclasificados competentes en inglés (RFEP): Estudiantes que previamente fueron clasificados como estudiantes aprendices de inglés pero que ahora han demostrado competencia en inglés.

Hablantes de inglés (EO): Estudiantes cuyo idioma principal es el inglés. NOTA : Es importante destacar que los programas DLE están disponibles para familias nuevas al país, así como a estudiantes de inglés recién llegados internacionalmente, que hablan el idioma objetivo del programa DLE, independientemente de su participación previa en un programa DLE. La clasificación de idiomas Se determinará la clasificación del lenguaje oficial del estudiante en la escuela después de la inscripción. ¿QUÉ TIPOS DE PROGRAMAS DE EDUCACIÓN DE LENGUAJE DUAL EST ÁN DISPONIBLES YQUIÉN ES ELEGIBLE?

El distrito ofrece tres programas de Educación en Dos Idiomas: Inmersión Bidireccional, Inmersión Unidireccional e Inmersión en Lenguaje Mundial, y en la escuela secundaria, ofrecen clases de lenguas y culturas mundiale. INFORMACIÓN DE LAS ESCUELAS DE ESTUDIOS AVANZADOS 55 ¿QUÉ SON LAS ESCUELAS DE ESTUDIOS AVANZADOS? Las Escuelas de Estudios Avanzados (SAS, por sus siglas en inglés) son escuelas del Distrito Unificado de Los Ángeles que han recibido una designación por sus programas equitativos y ejemplares de Educación para Alumnos Dotados y T alentosos (GA TE, por sus siglas en inglés). ¿CUÁLES SON LOS OBJETIVOS DEL PROGRAMA EDUCATIVO? Todas las escuelas del Distrito Unificado de Los Ángeles tienen programas GA TE para los grados K–12, diseñados para apoyar a los

alumnos dotados, talentosos y de nivel avanzado. Como modelos ejemplares de GA TE, las escuelas SAS ayudan a los alumnos dotados y de nivel avanzado a alcanzar su máximo potencial mediante una enseñanza diferenciada que incorpora profundidad, complejidad, novedad y aceleración. Las escuelas SAS también ofrecen entornos de aprendizaje estimulantes y de apoyo, fomentan la participación de las familias en el programa GA TE y brindan capacitación profesional continua a los maestros, enfocándose en las necesidades académicas y socioemocionales únicas de alumnos dotados, talentosos y avanzados provenientes de diversos entornos.

¿QUIÉN ES ELEGIBLE? Para participar, se debe verificar que los alumnos cumplan con los criterios de elegibilidad y indicaciones de SAS. Los criterios detallados están disponibles en choices.lausd.net y gate.lausd.org. Los alumnos de los grados Pre-K-11 que residen dentro del área de asistencia de una escuela SAS pueden inscribirse sin necesidad de presentar una solicitud a través del proceso Opciones; estos alumnos son incluidos automáticamente en el programa SAS/GA TE de la escuela si cumplen con los criterios SAS. Los alumnos de los grados Pre-K-11 que viven fuera del área de asistencia de una escuela SAS, pero dentro de los límites de Distrito Unificado de Los

Ángeles, pueden solicitar mediante el proceso Opciones si cumplen con los criterios SAS. Los solicitantes que no asisten actualmente a una escuela del Distrito Unificado de Los Ángeles—incluidas escuelas privadas y escuelas chárter independientes—deben presentar una solicitud y el formulario de verificación requerido antes de la fecha límite. Aquellos solicitantes que no estén inscritos en una escuela, programa preescolar o de kindergarten transicional (TK), o que estén inscritos en una escuela privada en el hogar (bajo declaración jurada de escuela privada), deben presentar una solicitud y enviar un correo electrónico a Programas para Alumnos

Dotados/T alentosos (GA TE@lausd.net) antes de la fecha límite para solicitar la verificación. CRITERIOS DE ELEGIBILIDAD SAS PARA KINDERGARTEN Los solicitantes que ingresan a kindergarten deben demostrar sólidas habilidades de pensamiento y resolución de problemas. La elegibilidad debe ser verificada por un administrador de preescolar o de TK utilizando los criterios de preparación para kindergarten de SAS. Los criterios detallados y indicaciones están disponibles en gate.lausd.org. Los solicitantes que no estén inscritos en preescolar o TK deben presentar una solicitud y enviar un correo electrónico a Programas para Alumnos Dotados/T alentosos (GA TE@

lausd.net) antes de la fecha límite para solicitar la verificación. ¿CÓMO SE SELECCIONA ALOS ALUMNOS? Se da prioridad a los estudiantes que residen dentro de los límites de la escuela SAS. Si hay espacios disponibles, se pueden seleccionar solicitantes elegibles de fuera de los límites escolares a través del proceso Opciones. Si el número de solicitantes elegibles supera los espacios disponibles, se llevará a cabo un proceso de selección aleatorio e imparcial. Los solicitantes que tengan hermanos actualmente continúan sus estudios en la escuela tienen prioridad, si hay espacios disponibles.

¿CÓMO SOLICITO AUNA ESCUELA CHARTER AFILIADA OZONAS DE OPCIÓN CON LA DESIGNACIÓN DE SAS? Algunas Escuelas Charter Afiliadas y Zonas de Opción (ZOC, por sus siglas en inglés) tienen la designación SAS. Las solicitudes deben presentarse a través del proceso correspondiente a las Escuelas Charter Afiliadas o a las ZOC. Los alumnos seleccionados o asignados a la escuela que cumplan con los criterios de elegibilidad de SAS serán incluidos en el programa GA TE/SAS de la escuela, a menos que el padre, madre o tutor legal decida lo contrario.

LAS ACADEMIAS SAS DE UN SOLO GÉNERO 59 ¿QUÉ SON LAS ACADEMIAS SAS DE UN SOLO GÉNERO? Estas escuelas están diseñadas para alumnos dotados, avanzados y altamente motivados de los grados 6 a 12. Los alumnos tienen acceso a cursos de Colocación Avanzada (AP), cursos universitarios de doble inscripción y oportunidades de preparación universitaria que fomentan la aptitud para la universidad y la carrera profesional.

 Desarrollarán habilidades de liderazgo colaborativo y compasivo  Fomentarán un profundo sentido de autoconciencia y conexión con la comunidad  Adoptarán un liderazgo ético y un compromiso con la equidad y la integridad  Vivirán los valores fundamentales de excelencia, liderazgo y bienestar en todos los aspectos de su experiencia escolar # ¿QUIÉN ES ELEGIBLE? LOS PROGRAMAS DE HONORES INDIVIDUALIZADOS 60 ¿QUÉ SON LOS PROGRAMAS DE HONORES INDIVIDUALIZADOS? Algunas Escuelas de Estudios Avanzados (SAS) ofrecen un camino de alto nivel académico denominada el Programa de Honores Individualizado (IHP , por sus siglas en inglés) para alumnos de escuela intermedia que demuestran un rendimiento académico de dos a tres niveles por encima de su grado actual en las materias fundamentales. El IHP se creó para atender las necesidades particulares de alumnos dotados, altamente dotados y académicamente avanzados que están preparados para experiencias de aprendizaje que

trascienden los programas de honores típicos de la escuela intermedia. Se espera que los alumnos estén listos para un currículo de estudios riguroso, altamente acelerado y/o compactado en las áreas de inglés, matemáticas, historia y ciencias. ¿CUÁLES SON LOS OBJETIVOS DEL PROGRAMA EDUCATIVO? El programa educativo IHP está diseñado para desafiar y acelerar los resultados de aprendizaje de los alumnos con un rendimiento de dos o tres niveles por encima de su grado actual en las materias fundamentals mediante:  El desarrollo de la capacidad de los alumnos para analizar críticamente la información a través de una perspectiva de profundidad y

complejidad  La involucración de los alumnos en un aprendizaje basado en la investigación que enfatiza la escucha activa, el rigor y la comprensión profunda  La promoción de una reflexión significativa y el aprendizaje colaborativo.  El cultivo del respeto hacia diversas perspectivas, intereses y talentos ¿QUIÉN ES ELEGIBLE? Para participar en el proceso de selección del IHP , los solicitantes deben cumplir con los criterios de elegibilidad de SAS y obtener una puntuación válida en la evaluación del IHP . Los criterios detallados y indicaciones están disponibles en choices.lausd.net y gate.lausd.

org. Para verificar que los alumnos tengan un rendimiento de dos o tres grados superiores, la evaluación del IHP incluye ejercicios de respuesta escrita en matemáticas y artes del lenguaje de inglés, así como pruebas de pensamiento crítico y resolución de problemas. Todos los solicitantes al IHP que presenten su solicitud a tiempo serán invitados a participar en una evaluación presencial que se llevará a cabo en diciembre. Se contactará directamente a los solicitantes con información detallada sobre la evaluación. Es la responsabilidad del padre/tutor revisar y seguir todos los procedimientos de verificación de elegibilidad antes de la fecha límite.

INFORMACIÓN DE LAS ESCUELAS CHARTER AFILIADAS 64 ¿QUÉ SON LAS ESCUELAS CHARTER AFILIADAS (AFFILIA TED CHARTER SCHOOLS)? Las Escuelas Charter Afiliadas son escuelas públicas operadas por el distrito escolar. Estas escuelas obtuvieron el estatus de escuela autónoma mediante un proceso de petición aprobado por la Junta de Educación del Distrito Escolar Unificado de Los Ángeles (Los Angeles Unified School District). Siguen las políticas del distrito, al mismo tiempo que cuentan con mayor flexibilidad y una mayor capacidad para tomar decisiones a nivel local. ¿CUÁLES SON LOS OBJETIVOS DEL PROGRAMA EDUCA TIVO?

Cada Escuela Charter Afiliada tiene sus propios objetivos educativos, los cuales están establecidos en la carta constitutiva (charter) de la escuela. Para obtener más información sobre los programas y objetivos de una escuela, comuníquese directamente con la escuela o visite su sitio web. ¿QUIÉN ES ELEGIBLE? Las familias que viven dentro del área de asistencia de la escuela no necesitan presentar una solicitud. Pueden inscribir a sus hijos directamente en la escuela en Enroll.LAUSD.net. Las familias que viven fuera del área de asistencia de la escuela deben presentar una solicitud a través del proceso de solicitud de

Opciones en línea en Apply.LAUSD.net. Las familias que viven dentro de los límites de otro distrito escolar también pueden solicitar asistir a una Escuela Charter Afiliada. Información importante No se requiere permiso para asistir. No existen otros requisitos de elegibilidad para solicitar ingreso a una Escuela Charter Afiliada. ¿CÓMO SE SELECCIONA ALOS ESTUDIANTES? Paso 1: El padre, la madre o el tutor presenta una solicitud dentro del plazo establecido para participar en el Sorteo Público Aleatorio. Los padres, madres o tutores deberán:  Consultar las fechas y los plazos de la solicitud en Apply.LAUSD.net

 Decidir a cuáles Escuelas Charter Afiliadas desean solicitar ingreso.  Presentar la solicitud en línea en Apply.LAUSD.net Información importante Puede presentar solicitudes para varias Escuelas Charter Afiliadas. No existe un orden de preferencia ni clasificación entre las escuelas seleccionadas. Paso 2: Proceso del Sorteo Público Aleatorio Los estudiantes que presenten su solicitud dentro del plazo establecido participarán en el sorteo público aleatorio de cada escuela. El sorteo solo se llevará a cabo cuando el número de solicitudes sea mayor que el número de espacios disponibles. Las escuelas deberán:

 Publicar la fecha y la hora del sorteo público aleatorio en el sitio web de la escuela y en la oficina principal.  Llevar a cabo el sorteo público aleatorio en enero.  Seleccionar a los estudiantes de manera aleatoria según las prioridades de selección y los espacios disponibles. Las prioridades de selección para los solicitantes se aplicarán en el siguiente orden para cada nivel de grado: 1 Hermanos de estudiantes que continúan inscritos y que viven dentro de los límites del distrito. 2 Todos los demás estudiantes que viven dentro de los límites del

distrito. 3 Hermanos de estudiantes que continúan inscritos y que viven fuera de los límites del distrito. 4 Todos los demás estudiantes que viven fuera de los límites del distrito. Información Importante Las familias no necesitan asistir al sorteo público aleatorio. Los padres también pueden consultar las Preguntas Frecuentes (FAQ) sobre las Escuelas Charter Afiliadas disponibles en Choices.LAUSD.net para obtener información más detallada. Los estudiantes que no sean seleccionados en el sorteo serán colocados en una lista de espera durante un año escolar.

When is the on-time application period? The application window opens October 1–November 6, 2026. Families may apply online at Apply.lausd.net .
Are on-time applications processed on a first-come-first-served basis? No. Applications received during the on-time application period will be processed after the application window closes.

What if there are more applications than seats available for a program? A random, unbiased selection process will be conducted centrally and students will be placed in accordance with the selection priorities.

What is the application and eligibility processes for Early/Middle Colleges? All students residing within and outside Los Angeles Unified are welcome to apply to Early/Middle Colleges (EMC). Applicants to Vladovic Harbor Teacher Preparatory Academy (VHTPA) must receive an eligible score on a Dual Enrollment assessment to be included in the VHTPA selection process. This assessment is the tool used to verify that students are performing two to three grade levels above, with multiple choice and written responses test items in mathematics, English Language Arts, critical thinking, and problem –solving skills. Students should prepare by engaging in CA content standards beyond current grade level expectations. On time VHTPA applicants will be contacted directly by the school to provide assessment information.

What if a student doesn't submit an application within the on-time application period of Oct. 1 - Nov. 06 and wants to enroll in an EMC? They may apply during the late application period, which begins December 1, 2026. Students will be placed in the order the applications are received based on space availability.
Will families be allowed to submit a paper application during the on-time application window? Only online applications will be accepted during the on-time application window.
Should a school accept a paper application? No. Schools will not accept paper applications.

If a student comes to enroll on the first day of school and there is space available, do they need to complete a Late Choices application? Yes. All new students participating in an EMC must submit a Choices application.
Do students currently enrolled in an EMC need to re-apply? No. Only students changing schools need to re-apply.
Since families are applying through the Choices application, will EMC applicants accrue points? No. Only students applying for Magnet programs will accrue Magnet Priority Points.
How many EMCs may a family apply for using the on-time application? Families may only apply to one EMC.
What if a family doesn't have access to a computer? Families may access smart phones, school computers, public libraries, Welcome Centers at Regions or parent centers to apply online.

Can a student accept a seat in multiple programs and schools? No. The family will have until the acceptance deadline to accept one program that is best suited for their child. Once a student has accepted a program, they will be removed from all other programs but will remain on the waitlist for each of the other programs to which they were not selected.
What if space becomes available? If space becomes available, EMCs are responsible for contacting applicants who are next on the waiting list and offering the students a seat at the school.

Will students living outside LAUSD boundaries need an Inter-District permit to attend an EMC school? Yes. EMC welcomes students living outside LAUSD boundaries. Please contact the EMC school directly for more information.

What are the Selection priorities for the Early/Middle Colleges? Schools select students based on the following priorities: Siblings of current students who reside within LAUSD boundaries (who will attend the same school). Students living within LAUSD boundaries. Siblings of current students who reside outside LAUSD boundaries (who will attend the same school). Students living outside LAUSD boundaries.

Will transportation be provided for EMC students? While transportation is not guaranteed for EMC, families may be provided with transportation depending on district route availability. Contact the transportation division for more information.
Who can I contact for additional questions? Please contact the Choices Support Line at (213) 241-4177. Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ) | Affiliated Charter Schools

What are affiliated charter schools? Affiliated charter schools are public schools operated by the district. These schools became charter schools through a petition process approved by the Los Angeles Unified School District's Board of Education. They follow district policies while also having more flexibility and greater local decision-making.

Who can attend an affiliated charter school? Any student who lives in California can apply to an affiliated charter school. Parents who live in the school attendance boundary do not apply and directly contact the school for enrollment. Parents who live outside of the school attendance boundary apply through the CHOICES application at Apply.lausd.net for grades Transitional Kindergarten (TK) - 12th grade.

If I apply for an affiliated charter school and live outside of the L.A. Unified School District boundaries, do I need a permit? It is not necessary to use an inter-district permit to apply for admission to an affiliated charter school. If you live within California, you may apply online at Apply.lausd.net .

Do students that live in the school’s attendance boundary need to apply through CHOICES? No, students who live in the affiliated charter school’s resident attendance boundary do not apply through CHOICES. Students that live in the attendance boundary go directly to the affiliated charter school to enroll. Parents can use the School Explorer at explore.lausd.org to see if their address is within the resident attendance boundary.

How are students selected for admission to an affiliated charter school? Parents apply during the on-time application window online. They can apply to multiple affiliated charter schools without a preference order. If the number of students who wish to attend exceeds the affiliated charter school's operational capacity, a public random drawing (lottery) will occur.

When and how will the public random drawing (lottery) be conducted? If there are more applicants than seats available, the affiliated charter school shall conduct its public random drawing during the month of January. Information regarding the date and procedure for the drawing will be posted on the school’s website and will be available in the main office.

I have a child already attending the affiliated charter school, will my applying child get a sibling priority? When the drawing is conducted, priorities are given to on-time applications in the following order: 1. Siblings of students attending and continuing at the school AND that also live within L.A. Unified (District) boundaries. 2. All other applicants that live within District boundaries. 3. Siblings of students attending and are continuing at the school and do not live within District boundaries. 4. All other applicants that do not live within District boundaries.

I have applied for siblings that share the same birth date (twins, triplets, etc.). What happens if one gets selected in the public random drawing and the other does not? Multiple-birth applicants (e.g., twins, triplets) that reside at the same address and apply to the same program in the same year will be placed consecutively in the CHOICES selection process.

Will there be any changes to how parents apply if my affiliated charter school is also a magnet, SAS, or dual language education program? Parents will continue to apply to magnet programs and magnet centers through the CHOICES brochure as they have always done. For SAS or dual language education programs at an affiliated charter school, parents first apply and must be accepted into the affiliated charter school. After a student is selected through the affiliated charter school process, the student may participate in the SAS gifted/talented program or Dual Language Program if they meet the program's eligibility criteria.
Who is responsible for notifying parents of their selection and waitlist status? CHOICES will send selection/waitlist letters for on-time applicants in February.

What if I missed the on-time application window? The late application window will be available beginning December 1, 2026. Late applications are added to the waiting list in the order received. Parents that apply using the late application will only be contacted by the school if a seat is available and your child is next on the waiting list. Parents may contact the school directly to inquire about their status on the waiting list.

Can a child accept multiple placements? While a family may apply for multiple schools, be offered and waitlisted for multiple schools, a child/family can only accept one placement at a time. After accepting an offer of admission, if the parent receives another offer in the future, they can accept that new offer and the previously accepted placement will be changed to declined.

Can an applicant remain on waitlist(s) if they accept a CHOICES placement? Applicants will remain on the waiting list for all affiliated charter schools they apply to. Even if they accept placement to another affiliated charter school or other CHOICES program, they will remain on the waitlist for the other school on the application. Applicants will remain on the waiting list for one school year only.

Who can I contact for more information? Please get in touch with the school directly for information about a specific affiliated charter school's instructional program, goals, and public random drawing process. For assistance with the application process please contact the CHOICES helpline at (213) 241-4177 or email us at applyforschools@lausd.net . For general inquiries about charter schools, including independent charter schools, that are not part of the CHOICES application, please contact the Charter Schools Division office at (213) 241-0399. Is the Dual Language Education (DLE) program for English Learners? Yes. All students, including English Learners, benefit from Dual Language Education programs.

Are there any requirements to enroll my child in a Dual Language Education (DLE) program? All students may enter the program at any time in Transitional Kindergarten (TK)-1st Grade and continue in the program until the student culminates from the school. A target language verification will be required for students new to LA Unified and students wishing to newly enroll into a DLE program in grades 2nd-12th with no prior DLE experience. In some cases, a new student who has proficiency in the target language (Arabic, Armenian, French, Japanese, Korean, Mandarin, and Spanish) can enroll in a DLE program after 1st grade without taking the target language verification. Additionally, English Learners whose home language is the target language of the program, may enroll through Choices at any grade level without the target language verification.

Are Dual Language Education Programs the same as Two-Way Immersion programs? Yes, Two-Way Immersion is a Dual Language Education (DLE) Program. Dual Language Education is an umbrella term, which encompasses Two-Immersion, One-Way Immersion and World Language Immersion programs. A Two-Way Immersion Program is one of three different Dual Language Education programs offered at L.A. Unified. Two-Way Immersion Programs are designed for both English learners and English speakers, which impacts both enrollment processes and instruction.

What languages are available in L.A. Unified Dual Language Education programs? Currently, L.A. Unified offers Two-Way Immersion Programs in Arabic/English, Armenian/English, French/English, Japanese/English, Korean/English, Mandarin/English, and  Spanish/English in selected elementary, middle, and high schools. The program's goals are critical consciousness and sociocultural competency, bilingualism and biliteracy, and grade level academic achievement. The One-Way Immersion Program offers Armenian/English, Korean/English, and Spanish/English DLE programs in selected elementary and secondary schools. The program's goals are critical consciousness and sociocultural competency, bilingualism and biliteracy, and grade level academic achievement. Will students living within L.A. Unified boundaries need an Intra-District permit to attend a Dual Language Education program at a location other than their home school? No. Intra-District (within L.A. Unified) permits are no longer required for these programs.

Will students living outside of L.A. Unified boundaries need an Inter-District permit to attend a Dual Language Education (DLE) program? Yes. Will transportation be provided for Dual Language Education (DLE) program students? Transportation may be available for students participating in Choices programs. When do I need to apply? The Choices on-time application window is October 1 - November 6, 2026. If you miss the application window, the late application period begins December 1, 2026. Late applicants are processed on a first-come, first-served basis. (Students are placed in the order of their selection preferences.)

Are On-time applications processed on a first-come, first-served basis? No. Applications received during the on-time application period will be processed after the application window closes. Students are placed according to their enrollment placement preferences.

What if there are more applications than seats available for a program? An unbiased, electronic selection will be conducted centrally, and students will be placed in accordance with the priorities for attendance. Siblings of current students in the dual language programs have priority for attendance. If there are more applicants than spaces available for a given grade, students will be placed on a waiting list.
Will families be allowed to submit a paper application during the on-time application window? Only online applications will be accepted during the on-time application window.
What if a family doesn't have access to a computer? Families may access smart phones, school computers, public libraries, Welcome Centers at Regions or parent centers to apply online.

Will resident students have priority enrollment? Yes, within the application window. Resident students who apply during the on-time application window are selected after resident siblings. Resident students, who apply during the late application window, are selected after resident siblings and in the order; the late Choices application was received. The number of students who are selected depends on each school’s seat availability.

Do students currently enrolled in a Dual Language Education (DLE) Programs need to re-apply? No. However, a new application is needed for matriculating students and for students wishing to attend another DLE program school.
Since families are applying through the Choices application, will Dual Language Education applicants accrue points? No. Only students applying for Magnet programs will accrue Magnet priority points.

How many different school programs can I apply to? Parents can apply to all Choices programs (Magnet, PWT, Dual Language Education, International Newcomer Academies, Early/Middle Colleges, Schools for Advanced Studies, and Affiliated Charter Schools) in the Choices application. For Magnet, Dual Language Education, and Schools for Advanced Studies, you may apply for up to three choices for each program during the on-time application window.
How many programs could I be selected to? You could be offered a seat for all programs to which you applied. However, you may only accept one program by the March 5, 2027 deadline.
Who will I contact regarding Dual Language Education Programs? Please contact the Choices Support Line at (213) 241-4177. Frequently Asked Questions | International Newcomer Academies

Is the International Newcomer Academy for English Learners? The International Newcomer Academy is intended for English Learners designated per state definition as non-U.S. born and in the country for 0-3 years or less. The program is meant to support the acquisition of fundamentals of English and formal academic English as well as attain secondary content area requirements that meet college and career expectations. Language and content integration is a key element to the program.

Are there any requirements to enroll my child in the International Newcomer Academy? Yes, the International Newcomer Academy is intended for English Learners who are non-resident students and designated per state definition as non-U.S. born and in the country for 0-3 years or less. Students who are new to the U.S. and are interested in a rigorous, dynamic college preparatory academy, this is the academy for them. For information about how to apply to the International Newcomer Academy, please refer to questions 5 & 6.

Is this academy the same as other English Learner (EL) programs? The aspiration of this academy is to have our International Newcomer students acquire English in tandem with graduation/A-G requirements. In contrast to traditional EL programs, this academy serves students in an interdisciplinary fashion integrating English Language Acquisition and rigorous secondary subject matter. Traditional English Learner programs in secondary settings have a designated EL course for students and subject matter teachers are expected to integrate English Language acquisition in their subject matter courses. Rather, in this academy that design becomes interwoven into the rigorous curriculum of subject matter courses.

How does the International Newcomer Academy support the diversity of languages that are possible/present in the program? The approach of the International Newcomer Academy is a multilingual integration of culture and linguistic capacity of all students. Students acquire English as they acquire traditional high school subject matter content as well as A-G requirements for CSU/UC prerequisites. Teachers are prepared through dynamic professional development to leverage the students’ multilingual and multicultural capacities to assist the students in their learning. Irrespective of the home language, students will be exposed to globally relevant and collaboratively designed curriculum and content. Students of all languages can participate.

Will resident students apply using a Choices application? No. Resident students from Belmont High School and Bernstein High School must apply through Zones of Choice (ZOC). Families from Belmont High School and Bernstein High School will not apply using the Choices application. If a parent/guardian would like their child to attend an International Newcomer Academy (INA) within their ZOC, the parent/guardian must select that site as their first choice during the ZOC selection process. If a student is assigned to a designated INA site through this ZOC process and meets the eligibility criteria, the student must be accommodated in the site’s INA program. Placement appeals through the ZOC office will not be considered if the student did not select the INA site as their first choice on the ZOC application. Will students living outside the residential boundaries need an Intra-District permit to attend the International Newcomer Academy program? Non-residential students who apply with a Choices application for the International Newcomer Academy do not need an Intra-District permit.

Will students living outside of L.A. Unified boundaries need an Inter-District permit to attend an International Newcomer Academy program? Yes. Students who reside outside of L.A. Unified boundaries will need to complete an incoming Inter-District permit.

Will transportation be provided for International Newcomer Academy students? Transportation may be available for students participating in Choices programs. What if there are more applications than seats available for a program? The International Newcomer Academy accepts all qualified students, year-round.
Will families be allowed to submit a paper application during the on-time application window? Only online applications will be accepted during the on-time application window.

Whom will I contact in regard to the International Newcomer Academy program? Please contact the Choices Support Line at (213) 241-4177. Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ) | Magnet

What is the magnet program? Magnet programs are Court-Ordered voluntary integration opportunities available to students in grades K-12 living within L.A. Unified. Currently there are 333 magnet programs located throughout L.A. Unified.
Who can apply to magnet programs? All students living within the boundaries of L.A. Unified are eligible to apply, including English learners, special education, and gifted/talented students.

What is the difference between magnet and gifted? The magnet program is a court-ordered voluntary integration program open to all L.A. Unified students. Fifty-seven (57) of the 333 magnet programs available are Gifted or Highly Gifted programs. In order to apply to one of these 57 programs, students must first meet the eligibility criteria .
How do I apply for a magnet school? You may complete the application on-line at Choices.lausd.net beginning of October.

Can I apply to more than one magnet? Students may apply for up to three magnet programs. If the applicant is selected to their first choice, choice two and three are not considered. If the applicant is selected into any program of their choice, the student will not be placed on any waiting list. If there is no space available in any of their choices, the student will be placed on the waiting list for their first choice only.
How do I submit the on-time application? All on-time applications are to be submitted online.

What happens if I miss the application deadline? Parents may submit Late Applications. If space becomes available the school’s magnet coordinator will contact you. The Late Application does not guarantee placement at the school site.

How are students accepted into magnet programs? Students are selected based on the magnet program goal and are randomly accepted into magnet programs based on the number of priority points they accrue. The number of students selected is based on the number of available spaces at a particular school. Any student who sent in an on-time application, but was not selected, is placed on a waiting list for their first choice only.
Are students selected on a first-come first-served basis? No. The selection process is random and occurs after the on-time application deadline.
Is there guaranteed selection if I apply? No. Applicants are not guaranteed selection.

How do I know if my child was selected or not? You will receive confirmation of your child’s application after applying. You will be notified via the parent account as to whether your child was selected or placed on the waiting list.

What is my child's status on the waiting list? Your child’s status will depend on the number of openings at the school of application as well as the number of applicants. You may call the school to inquire about potential selection.

When will my child get called from the waiting list? Calls to students on the waiting list may begin as early as February and continue through the fourth week of the fall semester. Students may also be called in December to accept enrollment for the spring semester.

Do I have to reapply every year? Students who are currently enrolled in a magnet program do not have to reapply unless they want to change schools (this includes promotion to the next school level, such as elementary school to middle school or middle school to high school). If a student remains on a waiting list then the student should reapply. Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ) | Permits With Transportation (PWT)

What is the PWT program? Permits With Transportation (PWT) is one of L.A. Unified's original integration programs and was established as a Court-Order to provide students with integrated school experiences within our district. PWT school assignments are made by the District to one of the following schools: Revere MS, Portola MS or Taft HS. The PWT program does not provide transportation to magnets or any other choices program.

What do I do first if I am interested in PWT? First determine eligibility: Students who are in grades 6-12 during the 2027-2028 school year and reside within the following L.A. Unified resident school boundary sending areas are eligible to apply for the PWT program: Middle School Sending Areas: Audubon, Drew, Gompers, Harte Prep, Mann, Muir and Obama Global High School Sending Areas: Crenshaw, Dorsey, Dymally, Hawkins, Jordan, Locke, Manual Arts and Washington Prep.
Can I choose the school I want for my child? No, the District assigns a school to you. The PWT schools are Revere MS, Portola MS and Taft HS.

Why does the District select the school? Enrollment meetings are held annually to verify that space is available in schools. These meetings take place after the Choices deadline date. This makes it impossible to name PWT receiving schools before the accept/decline deadline of each year. In addition, Transportation patterns and bus stops have already been established; therefore, no new schools will be added. The current receiving schools are Paul Revere Charter MS, Portola MS and Taft HS.

Where will the student be picked-up? Transportation routes have already been established for the PWT program. You will be notified about transportation by US mail the week before the new school year begins. For information about existing bus routes please call (213) 580-2950.

Do I need to reapply every year if the student does not get in? New PWT applicants need to reapply on a yearly basis if the student does not get into PWT the first year. Once he/she is in PWT you do not need to reapply to continue to stay at the current PWT school. Provided that space continues to be available, PWT students may continue from middle to high school. However, matriculating students need to submit an on-time application and respond by opting-in by the accept/decline deadline or they will default to their resident school program.

If I have two children, can they both attend a PWT receiving school? Yes, if space is available and they reside in a PWT sending area and both applications are returned before the deadline date, both children could participate in the selection process. When space is available, the PWT program will assign siblings to the same school.
Do PWT receiving schools have waiting lists? Yes, PWT receiving schools have waiting lists if more students apply than there is space available at the school.
Do I have to transfer my child if I don’t want to? You do not have to transfer your child. You may decide that keeping him or her at their current school is the best choice.

What if my child is a special education student? If your child is receiving special education services, they must be implemented per the Individualized Education Program (IEP). The Division of Special Education will assist in making the PWT program assignment according to the child’s IEP and the District’s guidelines.
What kind of program will my child be enrolled in at the PWT school? Your child may participate in all programs and activities available at the PWT school.

May I participate in the school/community activities at the PWT school? Yes. Parents are encouraged to participate in advisory councils, school site councils, PTA, and other functions at the PWT school.

Do I still have to enroll my child at the PWT school when I receive my Selection notification? Yes. When you receive the Selection notification, contact the PWT school to get information about the school’s enrollment procedures.

When will my child get called from the waiting list? Calls to students on the waiting list may begin as early as February and continue through the fourth week of the fall semester. How do students who live within the SAS school’s attendance area participate? Students enrolling in grades K–12 who live within an SAS school’s attendance area can enroll without submitting a Choices application; these students are automatically included in the school’s SAS/GATE program if they meet SAS criteria. Contact the school directly for more information.

How do students who live outside of the SAS school’s attendance area apply? Students enrolling in grades K–12 who live outside of the SAS school’s attendance area, but within Los Angeles Unified boundaries, may apply through the Choices process if they meet one of the three SAS eligibility criteria. For information regarding verification of eligibility requirements click here .

Can I apply to more than one SAS school? Yes. Students may apply to up to three SAS schools for the on-time application period. In addition, students may apply for one or all Individualized Honors Programs (IHP) and SAS Single Gender Academies, as applicable.

How does the SAS selection and waiting list process work for on-time applications? If a student is selected for their first-choice SAS school, their second and third-choice SAS schools will not be considered. If a student is selected for any of their SAS choices, they will not be placed on a waiting list. If there is no space available at any of their SAS choices, the student will be placed on the waiting list for their first-choice SAS school only. Each Individualized Honors Program (IHP) and SAS Single Gender Academy uses a separate random, unbiased selection process. A student who is not selected for one of these schools is placed on the school’s waiting list.

What if the SAS school is an Affiliated Charter School? Affiliated Charter Schools follow state and District rules for student selection, enrollment, and placement. If a student is selected through the Affiliated Charter process and meets one of the SAS eligibility criteria, the student must be placed in the school’s SAS/GATE program. More information is available in the Affiliated Charter Schools section of the Choices website.

What if the SAS school is in a Zone of Choice (ZOC)? Students who want to attend an SAS school within their Zone of Choice (ZOC) must select that school during the ZOC process. If a student is assigned to an SAS school through ZOC and meets one of the SAS eligibility criteria, the student must be placed in the school’s SAS/GATE program. More information is available in the ZOC section of the Apply website apply.lausd.net .

What is the difference between SAS and Individualized Honors Programs (IHP)? Both Schools for Advanced Studies (SAS) and Individualized Honors Programs (IHP) support gifted, highly gifted, and academically advanced students. SAS schools provide differentiated instruction with an emphasis on depth, complexity, novelty, and acceleration. Students applying to an SAS school must meet one of the three SAS eligibility criteria. IHP provides a more accelerated and rigorous curriculum than traditional honors classes. IHP is a high honors pathway designed for students performing two to three grade levels above in core academic subjects. In addition to meeting one of the three SAS eligibility criteria, students must also earn a qualifying score on the IHP assessment.

How can my child prepare for the Individualized Honors Programs (IHP) assessment? Students may prepare by engaging with rigorous California standards-based content that supports advanced thinking beyond current grade level expectations. Students may also practice how to explain their thinking, justify responses with evidence from a text, and solve complex problems through written mathematical reasoning. Families may review the California Content Standards at cde.ca.gov/be/st/ss/ .

What is the difference between SAS and Gifted Magnet? Schools for Advanced Studies (SAS) are highly effective GATE instructional programs offered at designated neighborhood schools. Gifted Magnets are voluntary integration programs coordinated by Student Integration Services. SAS, Gifted Magnets, and Highly Gifted Magnets all provide advanced learning opportunities with differentiated instruction that emphasizes depth, complexity, novelty, and acceleration. The eligibility requirements for SAS and Gifted Magnets are the same. However, Highly Gifted Magnets require students to qualify as Highly Gifted (HG) or Highly Gifted Applicable (HGA) through an LAUSD Intellectual Ability assessment. Is selection guaranteed? No. Applying or meeting the eligibility criteria do not guarantee selection.

Do students need to apply every year? Students already attending an SAS school do not need to reapply unless they want to change schools.
